skill.name: geo-scan
skill.description: Use when auditing a website or build output for deterministic content-readiness regressions and evidence-bounded discovery checks
skill.summary: Run deterministic content-readiness audits for websites and local build output.
skill.author: cucuwang

security_audit.summary: One finding is confirmed because the workflow invokes an external package through npx, which may download and execute package code. Five findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences or inline code formatting, and no semantic threats were found.

remediation.issue: The workflow runs geoptimize through npx without pinning a reviewed package version.
remediation.suggestion: Pin geoptimize to a reviewed version and require user confirmation before first execution or any network-based URL scan.

content.value_statement: Content and build changes can introduce hidden discovery and structured-data regressions. This skill runs geoptimize and presents deterministic findings with clear evidence and limitations.
actual_capabilities: Runs deterministic geoptimize scans against a URL, file, or local build directory.
Requests machine-readable scan output for reliable downstream processing.
Reports the score, methodology version, critical findings, and heuristic limitations.
Prioritizes sourced claims, noindex directives, structured-data problems, and reproducible regressions.
Can request an experimental multi-model review when the user explicitly asks.
limitations: A higher scan score does not prove improved ranking, indexing, visibility, or citation.
Experimental model reviews are subjective and remain separate from the deterministic score.
FAQ content and llms.txt do not affect the score.
URL scans depend on authorized access and must not bypass access controls.

use_cases.title: Review a production website
use_cases.description: Scan a public URL and summarize content-readiness issues before a search or discovery review.

use_cases.title: Check a local release build
use_cases.description: Audit generated files for noindex mistakes, structured-data defects, and repeatable content regressions before deployment.

use_cases.title: Track audit regressions
use_cases.description: Produce deterministic, machine-readable results that teams can compare across releases.

prompt_templates.title: Scan a website
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a deterministic content-readiness scan for [URL]. Summarize the score, methodology version, critical findings, evidence, and limitations.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a clear audit of one authorized public website.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a local build
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan [directory] as a local build. Prioritize noindex directives, unsupported claims, structured-data defects, and reproducible content regressions.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer wants to review generated output before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate a release regression
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan [current build] and compare the deterministic findings with [baseline report]. Identify new critical issues and explain the supporting evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs a repeatable release quality check.

prompt_templates.title: Add an experimental review
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the deterministic scan for [target], then add the requested multi-model review. Keep subjective conclusions separate and state that they do not predict visibility.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user explicitly requests a subjective model-based assessment.

output_examples.input: Audit the authorized production site and focus on critical content-readiness issues.
output: Critical issue: a noindex directive prevents discovery on the primary product page.
Limitation: the score does not predict ranking or citation changes.

output_examples.input: Check the local release build for regressions against the previous report.
output_examples.output: The build introduces one malformed structured-data field and two unsupported quantitative claims. Existing FAQ content does not affect the deterministic score.

output_examples.input: Add a multi-model review to the URL scan.
output_examples.output: The deterministic findings remain separate from the experimental review. The model opinions are subjective and do not predict indexing, visibility, or rich results.

best_practices: Use an authorized local build when a URL scan cannot access the target.
Keep deterministic results separate from experimental model opinions.
Verify that generated structured data matches visible content and current product behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not claim that a score increase guarantees ranking, indexing, visibility, or citations.
Do not bypass access controls when a URL scan fails.
Do not treat FAQ content or llms.txt as scored improvements.

faq.question: What targets can this skill scan?
faq.answer: It can scan an authorized URL, a file, or a local build directory through geoptimize.

faq.question: Does the score predict search ranking?
faq.answer: No. The score measures deterministic content-readiness checks and does not predict ranking, indexing, visibility, or citation.

faq.question: Can the output support automated workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow requests machine-readable output when another tool will consume the result.

faq.question: What does the audit prioritize?
faq.answer: It prioritizes sourced quantitative claims, noindex directives, misleading structured data, and reproducible content regressions.

faq.question: When should I use the multi-model review?
faq.answer: Use it only when you explicitly need a subjective review. Keep its conclusions separate from the deterministic score.

faq.question: Does llms.txt improve the scan score?
faq.answer: No. The workflow treats llms.txt as an unscored proposal and only offers artifact generation as an optional preview.
